title: Playable Web Game — Possible
description: A focused core loop, Three.js runtime, responsive controls, intentional game feel, playable build, and evidence report—made together and tested as one experience.

sections.heading: Fit
sections.text: 01 Fit Judge the outcome, not the category or agent skill list. Use this when A browser-game idea needs one complete, replayable Three.js experience. Core loop, game feel, controls, HUD, and runtime must be designed together. You value a finished playable build over a broad feature list. Not for A reusable game engine, level editor, or multiplayer platform. A conventional application that only happens to use Three.js. Publishing, analytics, or paid asset acquisition without separate approval.

sections.heading: Outputs
sections.text: 02 Outputs These are the inspectable deliverables. The expectation contract and evidence decide whether they make the promised outcome true. 01 Playable browser game 02 Game brief and tuning rules 03 Responsive HUD and controls 04 Production build 05 Evidence report

sections.heading: Expectations
sections.text: 03 Expectations This is the completion checklist: what must become true, how it can fail, and what evidence proves it. ! The build contains one understandable, replayable core loop with working start, play, win or loss, scoring, and restart behavior. Failure modes: Unclear objective; Prototype stops before a replayable result Evidence: Fresh browser playthrough; State-transition checks ! Keyboard, pointer, and touch-sized controls plus HUD, pause, mute, and reduced-motion behavior work on the declared profiles. Failure modes: Controls inaccessible on a target profile; HUD or audio settings do

sections.heading: Approval boundaries
sections.text: 08 Approval boundaries Outcome Pack approval permits local work only. External actions need separate approval. WHAT “YES” AUTHORIZES Saying yes authorizes repo-local agent skill installation, the shared outcome brief and state files, and local outcome work. External actions still require separate approval. Do not deploy, publish, purchase assets, or enable analytics without explicit approval. Do not use unlicensed third-party models, textures, fonts, music, or sound effects; record every external asset and license. sections.heading: Verification
sections.text: 09 Verification Completion requires evidence. Every run indexes its outputs, expectation results, decisions, repairs, approvals and limitations in one Outcome Record. 01 Run deterministic checks for scoring, collision, restart, pause, and game-state transitions where the architecture permits. 02 Use a fresh browser reviewer to complete the core loop with keyboard and touch-sized input paths and inspect console errors. 03 Measure loading and frame behavior on the declared desktop and mobile profiles; report observations without inventing performance guarantees. 04 Verify mute, pause, reduced-mo
